Subject: Observation: intermittent fiber at Orion DC - control/data implications

Hi team —

We saw a brief (~10-15m) fiber flap last night on the east pod (Edge Rack 7). This caused packet loss on one of the data paths and transient BGP adj loss to the control-plane management subnet. From our end it looked like data traffic retried over secondary links, but the control plane (management API, health checks) briefly registered as "unreachable" which triggered a small number of failovers on the customer's side.

Can Redwood review the attached annotated topology (high level) and confirm:
- Whether the control-plane traffic and the inference data-plane traffic are traversing physically separable links at Orion (diagram attached)
- What we should expect from the Redwood runtime re: KV-cache and prefix caching during such fiber interruptions (behavior, fallout risk)
- A short, actionable runbook we can hand to our NOC for triage (we'd like steps for "control-plane timeout" vs "data-plane degraded")

I've attached a quick sketch (orion_topology_annotated.pdf) and a short NOC note. Samir

--
Samir Patel
Network Operations Lead, Orion DataCenters
ops@oriondc.com

Thanks for the heads up, Samir — and for the annotated diagram. We're looking into the path separation and I'll pull together a short runbook draft for your NOC. Initial notes:

- Quick summary ask from our side: can you confirm which VLANs/subnets map to the management/control plane (API endpoints, KMS access, fleet health) vs the inference data-plane (gRPC/token egress)? The diagram helps but we need subnet annotations.
- From product/runtime perspective the important failure modes are: control-plane timeouts (RPC to control endpoints) and data-path jitter/loss (inference RPC retries). Behavior: the runtime will continue serving short-lived KV-cache sessions if the data plane remains intact; if control-plane becomes unreachable for longer than the control-plane heartbeat window we will attempt local fallback to pinned model variants (if configured).

Action plan (short):
1) Redwood will produce a 1-page runbook for NOC (Control-plane timeout vs Data degradation) — draft attached as runbook-draft-v1.md.
2) Internal: Jonas will validate the annotated topology and produce an egress/kv-cache impact matrix (attach).
3) Kimberly/Neha to confirm network subnet mapping from Orion and escalate if there are single points-of-failure.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00am ET to walk the diagram and agree on the runbook? If that's not convenient we'll take notes and circulate updates.

Attachments: runbook-draft-v1.md (draft), reference links.

Thanks — Avery

> Thanks for the heads up, Samir — and for the annotated diagram. We're looking into the path separation and I'll pull together a short runbook draft for your NOC.

Quick technical readout from infra/runtime:
- Control-plane endpoints use management VLAN 172.31.240.0/24 in the diagram; data-plane inference RPCs use 10.10.x.x under the edge subnet (please confirm exact prefixes). If those are accurate then physical layer separation exists but there are shared ToR uplinks in Rack 7 that may present a common-mode risk during a fabric flap.
- KV-cache notes: if the data-plane paths remain reachable the KV cache will continue to be used for in-flight sessions. However, if the control-plane (heartbeats, leader election RPCs) is disrupted for >35s we will mark control-plane unavailable and begin local safety fallbacks (scale-down, reject new long-running streaming sessions, flush certain ephemeral caches). That behavior is configurable by customer policies; we can recommend conservative heartbeat and fallback windows for your environment.

Attached is an initial "kvcache-egress-matrix.csv" that maps expected observable symptoms to operational checks (what NOC should see on tcpdump / health endpoint / telemetry) — this should map directly into your runbook bullets.

A couple of asks for Samir/orion ops before we finalize the runbook:
- Confirm exact management and edge subnets for Rack 7 (we need CIDRs).
- Any planned maintenance windows for the east pod this quarter?

I'll be on the call tomorrow; if you want me to prepare a short slide with fallback timing (35s threshold, 90s full degrade) I can do that.

Jonas
